body: This PR exposes a minor issue. It is possible to assign a Resource or Node to the wrong type. When dragging in two different Resources/Nodes with the same name it causes a script error. If the error is fixed by removing the first one, then the first one gets assigned to the var with the type of the second one. It doesn't seem to cause any problems. It gets saved to the tscn file, but when running it is just null and there isn't even any errors printed somehow. Ex. Drag "containers.gd" and "containers.tscn" to a script. It will generate ```gdscript @export var containers: GDScript @export var containers: PackedScene ``` and error. Remove the first line, and then the containers.gd will be assigned even though the type doesn't match. It seems like it shouldn't be possible `GDScriptInstance::set` since it checks the type, I'm not sure what's going on. It should be possible to check the types manually, probably with `ScriptInstance::get_property_type`. ~Or if we ensure the generated names are unique, that might also fix it.~ It can also happen when changing the type in some cases.

`ScriptInstance::get_property_type` just returns the Variant::Type, which will most likely just be `Variant::OBJECT`, so we probably need something else.

Regarding creating unique generated names for dragged variables, I have thought of doing that in a separate PR. However for `@export` variables specifically, that kind of creates an annoying workflow, since it would probably create something like `container_1`, which you would then want to rename, and that would reset the export variables value.
